intended_object: The standard group isomorphism R^× ≅ SO(H) between the units of R and the special orthogonal group of the hyperbolic plane. It sends t to the isometry diag(t, t⁻¹) in the isotropic basis. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition is built with `MulEquiv.ofBijective` from the homomorphism `hyperbolicTorus R : Rˣ →* specialOrthogonalGroup (hyperbolicPlane R)`. That homomorphism sends t to the linear automorphism that scales ![1,1] by t and ![1,-1] by t⁻¹. The file proves it is injective and surjective.

The objects involved are the right ones:
- `hyperbolicPlane R` is the form x₀² − x₁² on R², which is the hyperbolic plane when 2 is invertible.
- `orthogonalGroup Q` is the group of linear automorphisms that preserve Q.
- `specialOrthogonalGroup Q` is the subgroup of those with determinant 1.

So this is exactly the classical isomorphism SO(H) ≅ 𝔾ₘ(R). It holds over any commutative ring in which 2 is invertible; the surjectivity proof covers rings that are not fields.

The setting is not too narrow. The assumption that 2 is invertible comes from the library's diagonal model of the hyperbolic plane. Outside that setting, SO defined by the determinant is also not the right notion in characteristic 2, where one uses the Dickson invariant instead. Mathlib has no corresponding equivalence.
